dite_eq_ite.code:
dite_eq_ite.{u_1} {P : Prop} :
  ∀ {α : Sort u_1} {a b : α} [inst : Decidable P], (if x : P then a else b) = if P then a else b
dite_eq_ite.comment: A `dite` whose results do not actually depend on the condition may be reduced to an `ite`.
dite_eq_ite.description: This theorem states that when the result of a decision-based expression does not depend on its condition, it can be simplified to a standard conditional expression.

if_true.code: if_true.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} : ∀ {x : Decidable True} (t e : α), (if True then t else e) = t
if_true.description: This theorem asserts that when the condition is always true, the result of a conditional expression will equal the first option unconditionally.

ite_eq_right_iff.code:
ite_eq_right_iff.{u_1} :
  ∀ {α : Sort u_1} {a b : α} {P : Prop} [inst : Decidable P], (if P then a else b) = b ↔ P → a = b
ite_eq_right_iff.description: This theorem establishes that a conditional expression equaling the second option is equivalent to the condition implying that both options are equal.

dite_eq_right_iff.code:
dite_eq_right_iff.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} {b : α} {P : Prop} [Decidable P] {A : P → α} :
  (dite P A fun x => b) = b ↔ ∀ (h : P), A h = b
dite_eq_right_iff.description: This theorem shows that a decision-based expression equaling a constant value is equivalent to asserting that the condition implies the given function results in that constant value.

if_false.code: if_false.{u_1} {α : Sort u_1} : ∀ {x : Decidable False} (t e : α), (if False then t else e) = e
if_false.description: This theorem indicates that when the condition is always false, the result of a conditional expression will equal the second option unconditionally.

ite_eq_left_iff.code:
ite_eq_left_iff.{u_1} :
  ∀ {α : Sort u_1} {a b : α} {P : Prop} [inst : Decidable P], (if P then a else b) = a ↔ ¬P → b = a
ite_eq_left_iff.description: This theorem states that a conditional expression equals the first option if and only if the negation of the condition implies that the second option also equals the first option.

apply_ite.code:
apply_ite.{u_1, u_2} {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} (f : α → β) (P : Prop) [Decidable P] (x y : α) :
  f (if P then x else y) = if P then f x else f y
apply_ite.comment: A function applied to a `ite` is a `ite` of that function applied to each of the branches.
apply_ite.description: This theorem asserts that applying a function to a conditional expression is equivalent to creating a new conditional expression with the function applied to each possible result.
